QA vs Production · Structural & Schema Audit

Health Insurance page — new tech stack review

QA: seo.qa.policybazaarinsurance.ae/health-insurance/ Prod: policybazaarinsurance.ae/health-insurance/ Scope: HTML structure & schema parity, inline-CSS cleanup, visual diffs. Forms/lead-widgets excluded by request.
Bottom line: the new stack is structurally leaner and has better core SEO signals than prod in several places (richer JSON-LD, far less inline CSS, fewer images missing alt text, working hreflang). It is missing two content sections present on prod (Inclusions & Exclusions; How to File a Claim) and has not yet rebuilt several icon/illustration components — those currently render as plain text/lists instead of the styled card grids prod uses. Not pixel-parity, but a few of these are content gaps rather than just style, worth a product call.

2Structured data (JSON-LD)

Counted and parsed from script[type="application/ld+json"] on each page.

QAProd
Blocks present21
TypesBreadcrumbList, Product (w/ AggregateRating 4.8★/50 + 8 Review entries)WebPage only — headline, description, keywords
Schema.org protocolhttps://schema.orghttp://schema.org outdated
  • QA is a substantial upgrade here — Product/AggregateRating/Review markup is what makes star-rating rich snippets eligible in search; prod currently has no eligibility for that at all.
  • Verify with the content team that the 8 reviews in the QA Product schema are sourced from real, current customer reviews (not placeholder/migrated copy) before this ships — Google's review-snippet policy requires the on-page visible content to match the schema.
  • No Organization schema found in the page-level scripts on either environment (may live in a shared header/footer template not captured by this per-page check — confirm separately).

5Visual comparison

Full-page screenshots captured at 1200×650 viewport (@2x). Confirmed via scrollHeight that neither page double-renders — QA is 13,903px tall, prod 11,227px, each a single continuous render.

Hero / fold Visual gap
  • Body copy in the hero is word-for-word identical between environments — this is purely a component/visual gap, not a content gap.
  • QA's breadcrumb ("Home / Health Insurance") is visible in the hero and matches the BreadcrumbList schema in §2 — good, that's a real improvement over prod, which shows no visible breadcrumb.
  • Form CTA copy differs: QA says "Continue", prod says "Get a Quote" — flagging in case this is unintentional, though forms are explicitly out of scope for this pass.
"Why buy early" benefits section Visual gap
  • Same five benefit headings and body copy exist on both — again a component gap: the 5-card grid layout hasn't been rebuilt on QA, it currently renders as one image + a stacked list.

6Content sections missing on QA

  • Inclusions & Exclusions of Health Insurance in Dubai — full H2 section present on prod, absent on QA (confirmed in heading diff, §4).
  • How to File a Health Insurance Claim — 4-step illustrated process section on prod, no trace in QA's DOM.
  • "Directly from experts" advisor callout (named advisor photo + credential line) — present on prod near the top, not found on QA. Flagging since this is an E-E-A-T/author-trust element, not a lead-gen widget, so it's arguably in scope even under the "ignore forms" instruction — worth a call from the content side.

7Recommendations

  • Ship-blocking for SEO parity: add the "Inclusions & Exclusions" and "How to File a Claim" sections to QA before cutover — these are indexable content prod currently ranks with.
  • Confirm, don't assume: have content/legal verify the 8 reviews now in QA's Product schema are real and currently displayed on-page, given Google's rich-snippet review policy.
  • Quick fixes: set an og:image on QA; align the "Health Insurance Category in UAE" heading level to match prod's H3 (or decide QA's H2 is correct and leave prod as the outlier).
  • Visual backlog (non-blocking for SEO): rebuild the hero promo banner and the 5-card icon grid for the benefits section — copy is already there, this is component/CSS work only.
